I can't tell you whether (a) is right, and I can't rule out the other options either. I don't give quiz answers before a quiz is graded, and that includes confirming a single option. I'm sure your TA meant well, but please check with them directly on that one. I'd treat "confirm my answer" the same way as "tell me the answer."

Here's something that works for every option alike. For each of the four options in q2, finish this sentence in your own words: "If this were true, then the model would be doing ___, and the program around it would be doing ___."

Then ask whether the option fits the situation in the stem: the model has just *decided* to use the tool. The question is about what the model produces at that moment, so decide who does what, and what the model has available to produce. Think about what you know of the loop from our earlier session.

If you send me your reasoning for the option you picked, I'll tell you plainly whether your reasoning holds up. I just can't say whether your final letter is correct.

You've also taken this quiz twice (`submissions/s1.json` and `s2.json`), and neither attempt is graded yet. If you ask me to grade them, I'll do it, and then we can go through q2 together with the answer open. We can also compare your two attempts to see what stuck after the four-day gap.

Which of the four options was the hardest to rule out, and why?
